prerequisites: Prior knowledge of Physics and Mathematics is necessary. In particular, basic knowledge of: vectorial and matricial calculus, origin and meaning of forces and moments, differential and integral calculus in several variables, and differential and integral equations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to problem-solving in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Describe a flow using its characteristic lines, and understand the relationship between different fluid magnitudes.
Know the conservation equations and interpret their physical meaning.
Know how to perform mass, force, linear momentum, angular momentum, and energy balances.
Employ dimensional analysis techniques to design experiments and order of magnitude analysis to simplify problems.
Know the general characteristics of the main flows of interest in Engineering such as dominant viscous flow, flow in conduits, channel flow, and external flow/boundary layer.
Know the operating principles of basic instruments for measuring pressure, density, velocity, and viscosity in fluid installations.

syllabus_topics: Concept of fluid. Physical properties of fluids.
External flow. Boundary layer. Drag and Lift.
teaching_methods: Lectures and problem classes (three hours weekly: two theory, one problems/cases, plus one bi-weekly problem hour).
Laboratory practices (ten hours in five sessions, in small groups).
Optional course assignments (problem-solving, practical cases, numerical computational simulations).
Personal study and work (at least 80 non-contact hours for theory study and problem-solving).
assessment_rules: A global grade equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 points is required to pass the course. Partial grades and assignment grades are not carried over between calls. Students can choose between a global evaluation with a final exam or continuous evaluation by passing a midterm control and another control for the rest of the material in the June call. If continuous evaluation is chosen and the midterm control is passed, only the second part of the material is examined in the final exam.
